nodes.title: At the base of a bottomless pit
nodes.quote: That's where I am...at the base of a bottomless pit

teacher.text: The tantric baba's teaching comes back to him: kundalini lies coiled at the base, and to reach God it must rise.

nodes.note: The night before the trek, disgusted by the greed and blind faith around him, Dvij places himself at the very bottom.

nodes.title: The ancient temple of the forest
nodes.quote: his kundalini must have risen to the next level...that of svadhishthana

chakra.name: Svadhishthana
chakra.where: the sacral chakra, beneath the loins

teacher.text: The Kaula rites, 'the left path', follow the body in a spiritual universe.

nodes.note: After what happened at the ancient temple hidden in the forest, Dvij is sure his kundalini has risen a level.

nodes.title: A feast at Vidgati's shrine
nodes.quote: The effect reminded him of his kundalini that had risen up to manipura

teacher.text: "While life is yours, live joyously." The Charvaka host feeds them; Dvij names the feeling: hedonism.

nodes.note: Stuffed from the feast, Dvij feels his kundalini at the fire of the belly.

nodes.title: Kurup is gone
nodes.quote: If Kurup was Mahant's man, it means that Mahant knows about our expedition

party.text: Kurup has defected to the Mahant, taking his copy of the parchment. He is the one companion who falls through a flaw of his own: greed and treachery.

nodes.epic: In the Mahaprasthanika Parva, the Pandavas fall one by one on the ascent, each through a personal flaw. Kurup's fall fits that pattern exactly.

nodes.title: The field of fireflies
nodes.quote: Anahata! I can hear the sound of the unstruck
nodes.note: Under an ancient dolmen, beside the sleeping Bhavi, Dvij hears 'the sound of the unstruck': anahata, the heart chakra.

nodes.title: Yogini's gift
nodes.quote: And she left her dog as a gift to you, I suppose?

party.change: Yogini leaves; the dog stays with Dvij
party.text: The next morning Yogini has gone back of her own accord. Her dog stays, and from now on follows Dvij.

nodes.epic: The dog changes hands here, not at the end. In the epic, the dog that walks with Yudhishthira to the last is Dharma, whom some tellings link with Yama.

nodes.title: Chanting at the Vedic ashram
nodes.quote: Has my kundalini risen to vishuddha state?

teacher.text: The Vedas, the Upanishads, and the voice harmonising with the cosmos: "That you are."

nodes.note: Dvij only asks the question as the first drops of rain lull him to sleep. The book never answers it.

nodes.title: Ponga's work is done
nodes.quote: It's as if he has done what he came here to do

party.text: Ponga finishes the one task he came up the mountain for, sits against a tree and closes his eyes.

teacher.text: Under the tree by the Hanuman temple: "You seek the Absolute Truth. And yet you do not know that you possess it… You have to look within."

nodes.epic: The party narrows to Dvij, Bhavi and the dog.

nodes.title: Towards infinity
nodes.quote: My kundalini has risen to ajna, the brow chakra

party.text: Bhavi stays behind to lead the valley. Dvij walks on alone, and "the faithful dog followed him like certain Death."

nodes.epic: The solitary ascent watched over by a dog echoes the Pandavas' last journey. But Bhavi's parting is a handing-over of the mission, not a fall.
nodes.note: "There are seven extra-sensory chakras that reside above the head. I have to keep moving on. Towards infinity."

nodes.title: Sahasrara
nodes.note: Never reached. The book leaves the ascent open, and so does this rail.
